ai.description: The Medog skink reaches a snout-vent length of 6–7 cm. It is brown above with a dark lateral stripe and yellowish underside. Key features include smooth scales and a transparent lower eyelid window.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Medog Skink is best distinguished by its distinctively large, vertically elongated subocular scale that reaches the labial border, a feature absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: The Medog skink inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Medog skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky substrates during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphenomorphus courcyanus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Medog Skink (*Sphenomorphus courcyanus*) is found in the Eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting mid-elevation forest environments.
